dedupe_keys.name: data set seasonal variability in the global relevance of mountains to satisfy lowland water demand

description: Sarah Hanus and colleagues at the University of Zurich and IIASA publish simulation summaries, catchment information and Python analysis scripts on mountain runoff supporting lowland water demand. The August 2024 deposit is free under CC BY 4.0. The associated study covers 1990–2019 and river basins larger than 10,000 square kilometres worldwide, distinguishing essential from potential mountain contributions to lowland surface-water abstraction. The README separates model settings and time-averaged outputs, postprocessed basin statistics, mountain shares, catchment and population context, plotting tables and scripts. These materials can inform seasonal water-supply dependencies in regional allocation simulations. Additional raw simulation output is available only on request because of its size. No related catalogue record explicitly covers this analysis package. Spatial aggregation, model uncertainty and the distinction between essential and possible contributions limit direct application to individual utilities. Archives and numerical results were not independently checked.
